page.layout: One page, a title page centred in one column. Lines of title type from top to bottom, then a woodcut engraving with a Greek banner, then the printer's imprint, a rule and the date at the foot.

main_text.l: Animadversiones ad controversiam sextam Christianæ fidei,

page.notes: The woodcut in the centre (a figure with a sword and a scroll, within a decorative frame) carries a Greek banner whose letters are only partly legible, roughly "ΔΥΝΑΜΙΝ ΗΑΡΕΤΗΣ" along the upper arc and a few letters along the lower arc; the banner is not transcribed because the letters cannot be read with certainty. The handwritten "2" at the top right is not printed and is left out. The imprint date is printed in the old reversed-C form (CIↃ IↃ CIII), transcribed as MDCIII. The word "Auiso" in the italic line may be "Auviso" and "piacenole" may be "piacevole" (the Italian title is probably Avviso piacevole); I have copied the letters as they appear. The spelling "Ie-"/"su" is printed with a capital I before e, read as consonant J.
